title: Kyoto Temple Bans Visitors in Kimonos
paragraphs: Wearing a rented kimono while walking around Kyoto's historic streets has become a popular activity for many tourists. However, one temple in the city has now banned visitors who are wearing kimono from entering.

The temple, Seiraiin, is a sub-temple of Kenninji, Kyoto's oldest Zen temple, in the Gion area. It is known for its garden and for a huge painting of a white dragon on the ceiling of its main hall. After being closed to the public for many years, the temple reopened in 2024, and the painting has since become very popular on social media.

In July 2026, Seiraiin announced that visitors wearing kimono, Japanese-style clothing or costumes would not be allowed to enter. According to the temple, some visitors had been taking long, elaborate photos that disturbed people who had come to pray or to appreciate its art. In some cases, visitors had even stepped into the temple's raked rock garden or opened a sliding door without permission and damaged it while posing for photos.

Interestingly, the temple has said that its problem is not with kimono themselves. However, it explained that a large proportion of the visitors causing problems had been wearing them, so it decided the ban was a necessary precaution. Moreover, according to some people who saw the sign at the gate, the rule mainly targets "flashy" costume-style outfits, and visitors in everyday traditional clothing may be allowed in. The temple also says that it welcomes visitors who want to take photos, as long as they behave respectfully.

Seiraiin is not the only place in Kyoto to have problems with photo-seekers. In November 2025, its parent temple, Kenninji, posted a statement saying, "Our temple is not a photo studio, theme park, or similar facility." In addition, Gion has begun fining people who enter private streets in the area where geisha and maiko live.
So far, Seiraiin appears to be the only temple with a no-kimono rule, but other sites may be watching to see how it works.
